robot: two Franka Panda arms (7 joints each) facing each other across a table, panda-0 on the left and panda-1 on the right, each hand carrying the task's tool (or bare, with its two-finger gripper), torque-controlled behind jerk-limited joint servos

frame.suite: the scene's world frame (the table top is z = 0, z up)
frame.base_text: the scene's world frame, shared by both arms: origin on the table top (z = 0), +X from the left arm (panda-0, at the -X end, facing +X) towards the right arm (panda-1, at the +X end, facing -X), +Y left as seen from the left arm, +Z up; positions in the task text are already in this frame, and each arm's base pose is in describe_robot's spec_file (robot_spec.arms)

left.note: panda-0: carries the task's tool rigidly in its hand, so no gripper command is offered: closing the gripper below about 12 mm touches the tool's adapter and ends the episode; its aperture target stays as it is. The end-effector pose in the state is the tool's frame (as the task text defines it).

right.note: panda-1: carries the task's tool rigidly in its hand, so no gripper command is offered: closing the gripper below about 12 mm touches the tool's adapter and ends the episode; its aperture target stays as it is. The end-effector pose in the state is the tool's frame (as the task text defines it).

resets.note: Here: 3 resets in all (describe_robot: resets); the scene is rebuilt (about a second of wall time, no robot time) and only the last episode is graded.

notes: Each arm takes absolute joint-position targets (rad). Its servo turns every new target into a smooth, jerk-limited motion (the joints arriving together, at most about 1.4 rad/s on joints 1-4 and 1.7 rad/s on joints 5-7) and tracks it with torque control, so a far target is reached smoothly: move_robot with a short duration_s (e.g. 0.01) sends the goal as one target and lets the servo set the pace, a longer duration_s ramps the target. There is no end-effector pose command and no kinematics service: joints only. The scene moves by itself from the first control step, and robot time passes only inside calls that move or wait (10 ms per control step; observe with seconds 0 is free), so prepare a motion before sending it and use execute_trajectory (space joint, dt from 0.01 s) for timed sequences. Positions in the task text are world coordinates (base_text says how they map to the base frame). describe_robot's spec_file has robot_spec (base poses, joint, servo and safety limits) and proprio_groups for proprio_now (joint_pos, tcp_pose, joint_vel, gripper_opening, joint_effort, tool_pose: world frame, quaternions wxyz; target: the targets in force). Native rows (action type joint_position): per arm joint1..7 (rad) then the gripper aperture (m, 0 = closed .. 0.08 = open), panda-0 first.
